newsitem.title: UK: EU investigates CCSB over discount.
newsitem.headline: EU investigates CCSB over discount.

text.p: The European Commission is investigating Coca Cola & Schweppes Beverages (CCSB) for possible anti-competitive sales practices involving discounts to distributors, the Independent on Sunday newspaper said.
It said the Commission has asked several soft drinks companies to make formal submissions including their concerns about CCSB's rebates.
The competition directorate had complaints from pub companies, supermarkets and CCSB's rival bottlers during its review of the takeover of the company by Coca-Cola Enterprises, the article said.
"There are concerns that CCSB's discounts may discourage distributors from carrying other brands by insisting that they stock the company's complete product range," it said.
Three weeks ago, the Commission extended its inquiry for four months, giving little explanation. The vast majority of deals are approved by the Commission in about a month.
"The Commission's investigation will examine the impact of the proposed acquisition on the conditions of competition for soft drinks in Great Britain," it said at the time.
CCSB was a joint venture set up a decade ago between the Coca Cola Company and Cadbury Schweppes.

Under the terms of a deal announced in June, Coca-Cola Enterprises plans to buy Cadbury's 51 percent share in the venture and sign a new 15-year licensing deal to cover the bottling and distribution of Cadbury Schweppes soft drinks in Britain.
No one at Cadbury Schweppes was immediately available to comment.
